summary: Dan Arnold works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1996–2002) under scholars including Griffiths, Kapstein, and Pollock. His posts include McGill, Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Chicago (~2001).

Dan Ingalls studied at Harvard University (~1962–1966) and Stanford University (~1966–1968). Working in Indology and other fields, he held positions at PARC (~1972–1983), Apple (~1988–1996), Interval Research (~1996–2000), HP Labs (~2001–2005), Sun Microsystems (~2006–2009), and SAP (~2009).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Temple University (~1981–1989) and studied under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Mohanty, and Matilal, among others. He taught at Grinnell, Bates, Macalester, UCLA, Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Florida State, Boston University, Georgia, and Harvard.

Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University (~1984–1991) under Elliot Sperling and others. His career includes posts at Carnegie Mellon, the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters (~2000–2001), Hebrew University (~2001–2015), and Leiden (2005).

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis (~2000–2006) and served as Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity (~2012–2014).

Dan Zahavi specializes in philosophy. He earned a PhD from KU Leuven (~1990–1994) and a Dr.phil. from the University of Copenhagen (~1995–1999), where he became Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Center for Subjectivity Research around 2002.

Daniel A. Getz specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University (~1986–1994) under Stanley Weinstein, Ying-shih Yü, and Tairyo Makita, and later became an associate professor at Bradley University (~1994).
Daniel Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~2009–2013) under doctoral supervisor Jay L. Garfield.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol (~2002–2007) under supervisor Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1980–1987) and held positions at Butler University (~1987–1992), the University of Kansas (~1992), and Soka University (2002).

Daniel Borengasser works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Oregon (~2012–2014), where he studied under Akiko Walley, Charles Lachman, and Mark T. Unno.

Daniel Botsman is a historian and Japanologist. He studied at Australian National University (~1986–1990), Merton College (~1990–1992), and Princeton University (~1992–1999). He has held posts at Hokkaido University (~2001–2003), Harvard (~2003–2006), UNC Chapel Hill (~2006–2009), and Yale (~2009).

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. He studied at Indiana University (~1985–1990) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–1996) under Victor H. Mair, Paul Harrison, and Ludo Rocher. In ~2002, he joined Cornell University as Associate Professor.

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale University (1963) and Harvard University (1965), and held a post at the University of Washington (~1972–2006).

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Cambridge, Berlin, and Harvard. He held posts at Yale (~1856–1872) and UC Berkeley (~1872–1875), and served as president of Johns Hopkins (1875–1901), the American Oriental Society (1893–1906), and the Carnegie Institution for Science (1901).

Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1980–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held academic posts at Bates College (~1985–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–1989).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as director of research at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1981–2015) and held posts at the University of Lille and University Lille-III (~1988–2015).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard (~1932–1938) under Walter Eugene Clark, Willard Van Orman Quine, and Kalipada Tarkacharya. From ~1949 to 1983, he was Harvard's Department of Sanskrit and Indian Studies chairman.

Daniel John Gogerly worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as chairman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (~1838–1862) and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1858–1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago (~1966–1971). He held positions at Oberlin College (~1970–1973) and served as Professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2000).
